subject: history
title: European Aggression 1935-1938
welcome_lead: From Abyssinia to Munich, study Italian and German aggression and the failures of collective security.
meta_desc: History Move to Global War Adventure 2: Abyssinia, Rhineland, Anschluss and Munich.
final_note: You have walked through the 1930s crises. The lessons of appeasement remain central to international history.

walkthroughs.body_html: Mussolini's invasion of Abyssinia in October 1935 tested collective security. The League imposed limited sanctions but excluded oil and the Suez Canal. The Hoare-Laval Pact leaked in December 1935 discredited British and French diplomacy. Italy completed its conquest by May 1936 and abandoned the League.

Hitler reoccupied the Rhineland on 7 March 1936 against military advice; France and Britain failed to respond. The Spanish Civil War provided further opportunities for Axis cooperation. The Anschluss of 12-13 March 1938 incorporated Austria into the Reich. Each successful aggression made the next more likely.

Pressure on Czechoslovakia over the Sudetenland led to three meetings between Chamberlain and Hitler. At Munich on 29-30 September 1938 Britain, France, Germany and Italy agreed cession of the Sudetenland without Czech consent. Chamberlain promised 'peace for our time'; Hitler occupied the rump Czech lands on 15 March 1939, ending illusions about appeasement.

mcqs.q: What did the Munich Agreement actually achieve?
options: It returned the Sudetenland to Czechoslovakia.
It was a complete failure that achieved nothing.
Gandhi insisted on partition to ensure Hindu dominance.
It transferred the Sudetenland to Germany without Czech consent, bought time for British rearmament, and emboldened Hitler to seize the rest of Czechoslovakia six months later.
